newsitem.title: UK: Cobalt steady, largely ignoring Zaire strife.
newsitem.headline: Cobalt steady, largely ignoring Zaire strife.

text.p: European cobalt prices remained largely unmoved by continued unrest in Zaire on Tuesday, traders said.
Rebel forces since October 1996 have been in conflict with government troops and are now threatening to move deeper into the mineral-rich Shaba province
At present Zaire produces around 5,000 tonnes of cobalt and 40,000 tonnes of copper.
"Zaire is still not having a large impact on the cobalt market...it's been largely factored into prices," one trader commented.

They suggested that control of the hub of the mining region Lubumbashi by either side of the conflict was unlikely to inflict any long term damage to output of the hard currency earners cobalt and copper.
Cobalt after recent downside pressure is starting to climb against the backdrop of supply/demand figures, traders said.
Several suggested that demand would outstrip production against the backdrop of offtake from the aerospace industry and battery production.
"At the moment it is in the hands of how consumers will react to market fundamentals and their medium-term commitments.
Recently enquiry from end-users was at a low ebb but is starting to turn, traders said.
Any disruption of supply from Zaire is unlikely to impact on the copper market. Production from the central African state has fallen sharply from the 500,000 tonnes of output seen in the early 1980s.
Cobalt production has also declined owing to the lack of investment in existing facilities and the region's surrounding infrastructure.
Both cobalt and copper production has the potential to boom and possibly out do the dizzy heights seen in the 1980s.
But stability would have to emerge first.
"Any investment will come from foreign interests which are obviously reluctant to any financial commitment at the moment," a trader said.
On Tuesday high grade cobalt was indicated at $21/$22 a pound, unchanged from Monday but up on a recent lows of $19/$20.
Three months delivery copper on the London Metal Exchange was quoted around $2,335 a tonne, down by around $10 from Monday's afternoon close.
